text:
eric: Quick question about /v1/rank contract before I land client changes. Need a short decision on: score semantics (range/normalization), null/missing scores, and deterministic tie-breaking across replicas.

maria: we should be explicit. propose: returned 'score' is a float in [0,1] normalized per-request; if input scores provided, we normalize them. If none provided, treat all as equal (0.5) unless model returns scores.

jon: +1 on normalization. but we need to call out precision and stable ordering: floating precision means identical floats can still differ between runs. we should define tie-breaker fields.

tal: my preference: tie-break order = (explicit tie_policy header || candidate.original_index). default to stable by original_index so clients relying on deterministic order keep working.

eric: sample request I'm proposing for clarity:```json
{
  "query_id": "q_2026_03_17_01",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "payload": {"title": "A"}, "score": 0.87},
    {"id": "c2", "payload": {"title": "B"}},
    {"id": "c3", "payload": {"title": "C"}}
  ],
  "return_scores": true
}
```

maria: and sample response:```json
{
  "query_id": "q_2026_03_17_01",
  "ranked": [
    {"id": "c1", "score": 0.87},
    {"id": "c2", "score": 0.5},
    {"id": "c3", "score": 0.5}
  ],
  "tie_policy": "stable",
  "server_version": "r-infer-2.4.1"
}
```

jon: small nit: if we normalize to [0,1], how do we handle negative or unbounded model scores? we should document normalization formula: min-max per-request if input scores exist, otherwise apply logistic scaling?

maria: keep it simple: if clients send scores, do min-max normalization across provided scores. If model returns raw logits, server normalizes similarly before returning 'score'. If all scores equal or single candidate, return 0.5. Document ties.

alice: what about backward compatibility: older clients expect raw_score maybe. do we need an opt-out?

tal: add header 'prefer_raw_scores: true' for compat mode. default false. also expose 'raw_score' in response when present so we don't break observability for advanced users.

eric: agreed. decision summary to put in the API spec: 1) returned 'score' is normalized [0,1] via min-max per-request if scores exist; 2) if no scores, default 0.5; 3) tie-break default = stable on original_index; optional header x-rank-tie=lexicographic|stable|seeded; 4) include raw_score when available and when client requests prefer_raw_scores; 5) document float precision and recommend clients use deterministic id ordering if they need absolute stability.

jon: can we add a short example for tie edge-case? e.g., c2 and c3 both 0.5 and original_index decides.

eric: I'll add that to the spec doc and open a tiny PR. pinging @maria and @jon for quick review when ready.

infra-bot: deploy queued: /specs/ranking-contract -> staging (ci-passes).

maria: lgtm, just add the normalization formula snippet and a note about streaming vs non-streaming responses (streaming yields incremental scores but final normalization still per-request).

eric: will do. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/specs/pull/412 — please review. tagging for a 24h async review. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

alice: thanks — will review tomorrow. :thumbsup:

jon: one more: add test vectors (3 candidate cases: all equal, one higher, negative logits) so SDKs can assert behavior.

eric: good call. I'll include tests in the PR.

tal: mark as decision in api/CHANGELOG. once PR merged, I'll notify SDKs for minor bump.

eric: sweet. closing thread after PR lands.
